questions.q: In a class, ratio of boys to the girls is 5:3. If 20% of the boys and 40% of the girls fail an exam, what is the ratio of the number of boys who passed to the number of girls who passed? (CHSL TIER I - 21/11/2025 - SHIFT 1)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, boys 80% pass aur girls 60% pass hui hain. Seedha ratio $5 \times 80$ aur $3 \times 60$ ka nikalega, zeroes toh waise bhi kat jayenge.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Direct fraction product laga, faltu calculations mat kar. Mathematically :-

$5 \times 0.8 : 3 \times 0.6$

$4 : 1.8$

$40 : 18 = 20 : 9$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Base values ko 100 ke multiple mein maan le taaki decimals se bach sake. Mathematically :-

$B = 500, G = 300$

$P_B = 500 \times 0.80 = 400$

$P_G = 300 \times 0.60 = 180$

$400 : 180 = 20 : 9$

Exam Takeaway: Ratio questions mein hamesha direct multiplication kar. Ratio nikalte waqt percentages ke zeroes ignore kara kar, time bachega.

List IList II
Ratio % Shift Trick$R_1 \times \%_1 : R_2 \times \%_2$

questions.q: Doll's Math's test consists of 115 questions from three sections- i.e. A, B and C. 15 questions from section A, 40 questions from section B and 60 questions from section C. Although, she answered 66.67% of section A, 60% of section B and 50% of section C correctly. She did not pass the test because she got less than 60% of the total marks. How many more questions would she have to answer correctly to earn 60% of the marks, if each question's mark is 1?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, $66.67\%$ yani $\frac{2}{3}$. A, B, aur C ke sahi questions nikal aur 115 ke $60\%$ se compare kar le.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Direct parts nikal kar add kar aur target se subtract maar. Mathematically :-

$\text{Marks} = (15 \times \frac{2}{3}) + (40 \times \frac{3}{5}) + (60 \times \frac{1}{2})$

$\text{Marks} = 10 + 24 + 30 = 64$

$\text{Target} = 115 \times \frac{3}{5} = 69$

$\text{Diff} = 69 - 64 = 5$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Total questions aur percentages ko thoda detail mein evaluate kar. Mathematically :-

$A_{correct} = \frac{66.67}{100} \times 15 = 10$

$B_{correct} = \frac{60}{100} \times 40 = 24$

$C_{correct} = \frac{50}{100} \times 60 = 30$

$\text{Total Correct} = 64$

$\text{Req} = \frac{60}{100} \times 115 = 69 \Rightarrow 69 - 64 = 5$

Exam Takeaway: Percentages ki standard fraction values tips par yaad rakh, SSC CGL mein seedha 10-15 seconds bachenge.

List IList II
Crucial Fraction$66.67\% = \frac{2}{3}$

questions.q: Salary of A increased by 8% in the year 2015 as compared to 2014 and decreased by 6% in the year 2016 as compared to 2015. If his salary was Rs. 2,34,778 in 2016, his salary (round off to nearest whole number) in 2014 was:
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, $+8\%$ aur $-6\%$ ka net lagbhag $+1.5\%$ ayega. Agar value thodi badhkar $2.34$ Lakh hui hai, toh original pakka thodi chhoti hogi, options se seedha eliminate maar.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Successive formula laga aur options eliminate kar. Mazdoori mat kar. Mathematically :-

$\text{Net} = 8 - 6 - \frac{48}{100} = +1.52\%$

$101.52\% = 234778$

$\text{Base} \approx \frac{234778}{1.0152} < 234778$

$\text{Only option < 234k is 231263}$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Basic multiplying factor wali equation likh kar reverse aaja. Mathematically :-

$x \times 1.08 \times 0.94 = 234778$

$x \times 1.0152 = 234778$

$x = 231262.8 \approx 231263$

Exam Takeaway: SSC CGL intentionally aise options set karta hai. Exact calculation se pehle approximation se options hata, exam clear yahi approach karayegi.

List IList II
Successive Formula$x + y + \frac{xy}{100}$

questions.q: If 12.5% of p is equal to 50% of q, what is the ratio p: q? (CGL TIER I - 19/09/2025 - SHIFT 2)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, $12.5\%$ is $\frac{1}{8}$ aur $50\%$ is $\frac{1}{2}$. Dono ko aamne-saamne rakh aur ratio sidha tere samne aayega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Fractions me convert kar aur shift kar. Mathematically :-

$\frac{1}{8}p = \frac{1}{2}q$

$\frac{p}{q} = \frac{8}{2} = \frac{4}{1}$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Percentages ko solve kar equation banakar. Mathematically :-

$\frac{12.5}{100} \times p = \frac{50}{100} \times q$

$12.5p = 50q$

$\frac{p}{q} = \frac{50}{12.5} = \frac{4}{1}$

Exam Takeaway: Fraction conversions hamesha secondary steps ko eliminate kar dete hain.

List IList II
Base Conversion$12.5\% = \frac{1}{8}$

questions.q: The population of a town decreases by x% in the year 2020 and increases by 2x% in the year 2021. If the population of the city at the end of 2019 is 45000 and that of the city at the end of 2021 is 49536, then find the value of x.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, base 45000 hai aur final 49536 hai. Total change thoda sa positive hai, lagbhag 10%. Direct net percentage change nikal aur successive net-effect rule me option satisfy karwa.

Method 1 (Ultra Ninja Technique): Net percentage growth nikal aur successive percentage ka net-effect formula (A + B + AB/100) mind me set kar jahan A = -x aur B = +2x. Phir direct option se satisfy karwa.
Mathematically :-
$$ \frac{49536 - 45000}{450} = \frac{4536}{450} = 10.08\% $$
$$ -x + 2x - \frac{x \times 2x}{100} = 10.08\% $$
$$ x - \frac{2x^2}{100} \approx 10\% $$
$$ 14 - \frac{2(14)^2}{100} = 14 - \frac{392}{100} = 14 - 3.92 = 10.08\% $$

Method 2 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Option 14\% utha aur direct fraction multipliers laga ke digital sum ya last digits verify kar le.
Mathematically :-
$$ 45000 \times \left(1 - \frac{14}{100}\right) \times \left(1 + \frac{28}{100}\right) $$
$$ 45000 \times 0.86 \times 1.28 $$
$$ 45 \times 86 \times 12.8 = 49536 $$

Method 3 (Concept Builder): Pura basic equation set karke quadratic banani padegi jo time legi.
Mathematically :-
$$ 45000 \left(1 - \frac{x}{100}\right) \left(1 + \frac{2x}{100}\right) = 49536 $$
$$ \left(1 - \frac{x}{100}\right) \left(1 + \frac{2x}{100}\right) = \frac{49536}{45000} $$
$$ 1 + \frac{x}{100} - \frac{2x^2}{10000} = 1.1008 $$
$$ \frac{x}{100} - \frac{2x^2}{10000} = 0.1008 $$
$$ x = 14 $$

Exam Takeaway: Ultra Ninja Technique sabse deadly hai kyunki isme actual calculation 4536/450 nikalte hi option se seedha dikh jata hai. Exam me hamesha net change percentage se approach kar.

List IList II
Net Effect Rule$$ x - \frac{2x^2}{100} = \text{Net } \% $$

questions.q: In an examination, A got 25% marks more than B, B got 10% less than C and C got 25% more than D. If D got 320 marks out of 500, then the marks obtained by A were?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, jab bhi sequential ya chain mein percentage change ho (A se B, B se C, C se D), toh beech ke variables alag se nikalne ki zaroorat nahi hai. Sidha unka fraction ratio likh kar multiply maar de, B aur C apne aap cancel out ho jayenge aur direct First (A) aur Last (D) ka ratio bachega. Image me jo tune kiya hai, wahi exact ninja technique hai!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Ratio method lagakar sidha multiply kar de (teri image wali method). Mathematically :-

$$ \frac{A}{B} \times \frac{B}{C} \times \frac{C}{D} = \frac{A}{D} $$

$$ \frac{5}{4} \times \frac{9}{10} \times \frac{5}{4} = \frac{45}{32} $$

$$ \text{Here, } \frac{A}{D} = \frac{45}{32} $$

$$ 32 \text{ units } \rightarrow 320 $$

$$ 45 \text{ units } \rightarrow 450 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Peechhe se pakad aur individually backward chain solve kar (jab intermediate values nikalni pad jayein). Mathematically :-

$$ C = 320 + (320 \times \frac{1}{4}) = 400 $$

$$ B = 400 - (400 \times \frac{1}{10}) = 360 $$

$$ A = 360 + (360 \times \frac{1}{4}) = 450 $$

Exam Takeaway: Chain questions mein agar bas First (A) aur Last (D) ka aapas mein relation nikalna ho, toh unke Multiplier Fractions ko direct aapas mein multiply karna sabse fast approach hota hai.

List IList II
First to Last Ratio$$ \frac{\text{Initial}}{\text{Final}} = M.F_1 \times M.F_2 \times M.F_3 $$

questions.q: If 20% of X is added to 75% of X then the results become (X-21)% of 200 then find the value of 250% of X?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, LHS ban gaya $95\%$ of X. Aur RHS pe 200 ka koi bhi percentage seedha double ho jata hai. Ek line ki aasan equation banegi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Zeroes hata kar decimals ki sidhi equation bana aur target nikal. Mathematically :-

$0.95X = 2(X - 21)$

$0.95X = 2X - 42$

$1.05X = 42 \Rightarrow X = 40$

$Target = 2.5 \times 40 = 100$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Pura percentage solve kar step by step. Mathematically :-

$\frac{20X}{100} + \frac{75X}{100} = \frac{(X-21)}{100} \times 200$

$\frac{95X}{100} = 2X - 42$

$\frac{105X}{100} = 42 \Rightarrow X = 40$

$\frac{250}{100} \times 40 = 100$

Exam Takeaway: Percentage of 200 jaisi cheezon ko sidha multiply by 2 socha kar, steps likh ke time waste mat kar.

List IList II
200's % Trick$y\% \text{ of } 200 = 2y$

questions.q: Price of ticket in a circus increases by 33.33%, number of visitors reduces by 12.5%. Find effect on income?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, jab Price $\times$ Visitors = Income hoti hai, toh sidha ratio multiply method lagta hai. $\frac{1}{3}$ increment aur $\frac{1}{8}$ decrement ka net effect nikalna hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Initial aur final ratios ko seedha multiply maar. Mathematically :-

$\text{Price: } 3 \rightarrow 4$

$\text{Visitors: } 8 \rightarrow 7$

$\text{Income: } (3\times8) \rightarrow (4\times7) = 24 \rightarrow 28$

$\text{Change} = \frac{+4}{24} = \frac{1}{6} = 16.66\%$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Fractional change laga. Mathematically :-

$\text{Income} = (1 + \frac{1}{3}) \times (1 - \frac{1}{8})$

$\text{Income} = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{7}{8} = \frac{28}{24} = \frac{7}{6}$

$\text{Effect} = \frac{7}{6} - 1 = \frac{1}{6} = 16.66\%$

Exam Takeaway: $A \times B = C$ format wale saare sawal ratio multiply method se hi foda kar, best approach yahi hai.

List IList II
Ratio Multiplier$P_{ratio} \times V_{ratio} = I_{ratio}$

questions.q: In 2003, the total population of a village was 3650, out of which 42% were females. In 2004, the total population increased by 10% as compared to the previous year. If the number of females remained the same in 2004, what was the percentage increase in the number of males in 2004 as compared to 2003 ?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM/Deviation.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, logic laga! Agar population overall $10\%$ badhi hai aur females bilkul badhi nahi, toh jo total growth aayi hai wo *sirf* males ki wajah se aayi hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Growth value sidha nikal aur old males pe divide kar ke approximate kar. Mathematically :-

$\text{Total Inc} = 3650 \times 10\% = 365$

$\text{Old Males} = 3650 \times 58\% = 2117$

$\text{Male Inc } \% = \frac{365}{2117} \times 100$

$10\% = 211.7, 5\% = 105.8 \Rightarrow 15\% = 317.5$

$\text{Rem} \approx 47.5 \approx 2.2\% \Rightarrow 17.2\%$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Pura data calculate kar ekdum basic step se. Mathematically :-

$\text{Old Pop} = 3650 \Rightarrow F = 1533, M = 2117$

$\text{New Pop} = 4015 \Rightarrow F = 1533, M = 2482$

$\text{Inc in M} = 2482 - 2117 = 365$

$\% = \frac{365}{2117} \times 100 \approx 17.23\%$

Exam Takeaway: Absolute increase kis category me aa raha hai wo pehchan le, faltu exact multiply/divide me time kharab mat kar, options door door the.

List IList II
Logic Hack$\text{Total Inc} = \text{Male Inc}$

questions.q: The price of a commodity increased by 22%. By what percentage (correct to two decimal places) should its consumption be reduced so that the total expenditure remains the same?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: CPR.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, expenditure same rakhna hai matlab Price ratio ka direct reverse Consumption ratio hoga. 100 ki cheez 122 ho gayi, wapis 100 aana hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): CPR lagake sidha nikal. $\frac{x}{y}$ bada toh $\frac{x}{x+y}$ kam hoga. Mathematically :-

$P \uparrow \frac{22}{100} = \frac{11}{50}$

$C \downarrow \frac{11}{50+11} = \frac{11}{61}$

$\frac{11}{61} \times 100 = \frac{1100}{61} \approx 18.03\%$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Base 100 leke consumption reduce kar. Mathematically :-

$\text{New Price} = 122$

$\text{Reduction Req} = 22$

$\text{Red } \% = \frac{22}{122} \times 100 = \frac{1100}{61}$

$\approx 18.032\%$

Exam Takeaway: Inverse proportion ke concepts mein direct fraction adjustment (CPR) use karke base identify kiya karo.

List IList II
CPR Rule$\uparrow \frac{N}{D} \Rightarrow \downarrow \frac{N}{N+D}$

questions.q: Evaluate: 12.5% of 560 km + 66.66% of 240 km (CGL TIER I- 12/09/2025 - SHIFT 3)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, ye standard fractions ki checking ho rahi hai SSC taraf se. $12.5\%$ is $\frac{1}{8}$ aur $66.66\%$ is $\frac{2}{3}$. Seedha kata-peeti kar.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Fractions rakhte hi answer visible ho jayega. Mathematically :-

$\frac{1}{8} \times 560 + \frac{2}{3} \times 240$

$70 + 160 = 230$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Percentages ko manually divide kar (time waste approach). Mathematically :-

$\frac{12.5}{100} \times 560 + \frac{66.66}{100} \times 240$

$\frac{1}{8} \times 560 + \frac{2}{3} \times 240$

$70 + 160 = 230$

Exam Takeaway: Standard fractional equivalents yaad na hona ek crime hai. Inko chaat ja.

List IList II
Standard Fractions$66.66\% = \frac{2}{3}$

questions.q: In the year 2014, the population of a city was 30,000. The population of the city increased in 2015, 2016, and 2017 by a constant percentage of \(x\%\) every year. In the year 2018, if the population of the city was increased by 20% over the previous year, then the population of the city became 32,208 more than that of the year 2014. What is the value of \(x\)?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change (CI, Area, Successive discounts).

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, 2014 se 2017 tak 3 saal ka same successive growth hai (\(x\%\)). Uske baad 2018 me 20% badha. Seedha reverse gear laga! 2018 ki final value ko 20% kam karke (matlab \(\frac{5}{6}\) se multiply karke) 2017 pe aa ja. Phir Initial (2014) aur Final (2017) ka ratio leke seedha Cube Root pel de. 3 saal ka gap = Cube Root. Khel khatam!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Reverse Ratio & Root Method.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Final } P_{2018} = 30000 + 32208 = 62208 $$

$$ P_{2017} = 62208 \times \frac{5}{6} = 51840 $$

$$ \text{Multiplier}^3 = \frac{P_{2017}}{P_{2014}} = \frac{51840}{30000} = \frac{5184}{3000} = \frac{1728}{1000} = \frac{216}{125} $$

$$ \text{Multiplier} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{216}{125}} = \frac{6}{5} \implies 20\% \text{ Increase} $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Basic Compound Interest approach (Tree Builder).

Mathematically :-

$$ 30000 \times \left(1 + \frac{x}{100}\right)^3 \times \left(1 + \frac{20}{100}\right) = 62208 $$

$$ 30000 \times \left(1 + \frac{x}{100}\right)^3 \times \frac{6}{5} = 62208 $$

$$ 36000 \times \left(1 + \frac{x}{100}\right)^3 = 62208 $$

$$ \left(1 + \frac{x}{100}\right)^3 = \frac{62208}{36000} = \frac{1728}{1000} = 1.728 $$

$$ 1 + \frac{x}{100} = 1.2 \implies x = 20 $$

Exam Takeaway: Method 1 (Ninja Technique) sabse best hai. Jab bhi time periods ka gap \(n\) saal ho, toh fractions ka \(n^{th}\) root nikalna sabse fast approach hota hai. Weighted average ya basic formula exam me lamba fasa dega.

StepAction (N years Successive)
Step 1Ratio banao = (Final Value / Initial Value)
Step 2Agar 2 saal ka gap hai -> Square Root
Step 3Agar 3 saal ka gap hai -> Cube Root

questions.q:
According to a localized census survey, the active demographic base of a metropolitan zone was recorded at 1,02,400 at the end of 2014. Driven by consistent industrialization, this base observed a uniform successive annual growth rate of \(x\%\) for the subsequent three years (2015, 2016, and 2017). The year 2018 witnessed an unprecedented migration surge, causing the population to swell by 35% over the preceding year. However, a sudden pandemic in 2019 triggered a demographic contraction of 10%.

If the final recorded population at the conclusion of 2019 stood at 2,43,000, determine the ratio of the uniform growth rate (\(x\)) to the net effective percentage change observed strictly from the beginning of 2018 to the end of 2019.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change (CI, Area, Successive discounts).

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, language kitni bhi bhayankar ho, structure simple hai. "End of 2019" ki final value (243,000) se hume "End of 2017" tak reverse gear lagana hai. 10% decline ka ulta \(\frac{10}{9}\) aur 35% jump ka ulta \(\frac{20}{27}\) (kyunki 135% = \(\frac{27}{20}\)). Ek baar 2017 ka data mil gaya, toh seedha 2014 wale base se ratio banake Cube Root pel dena hai. Aur jo second part pucha hai (2018-2019 ka effective change), wo directly successive formula \(A + B + \frac{AB}{100}\) se bina population value use kiye nikal jayega!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Reverse Gear & Ratio Masterclass.

Mathematically :-

$$ P_{2017} = 243000 \times \frac{10}{9} \times \frac{20}{27} = 200000 $$

$$ \text{Multiplier}^3 = \frac{200000}{102400} = \frac{2000}{1024} = \frac{125}{64} $$

$$ \text{Multiplier} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{125}{64}} = \frac{5}{4} \implies 25\% \text{ (Value of } x) $$

$$ \text{Effective } \% (2018-19) = 35 - 10 - \frac{35 \times 10}{100} = 21.5\% $$

$$ \text{Ratio} = 25 : 21.5 = 250 : 215 = 50 : 43 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Basic Successive Chain.

Mathematically :-

$$ 102400 \times \left(1 + \frac{x}{100}\right)^3 \times \left(\frac{135}{100}\right) \times \left(\frac{90}{100}\right) = 243000 $$

$$ \left(1 + \frac{x}{100}\right)^3 \times \frac{27}{20} \times \frac{9}{10} = \frac{243000}{102400} $$

$$ \left(1 + \frac{x}{100}\right)^3 = \frac{2430}{1024} \times \frac{200}{243} = \frac{2000}{1024} $$

$$ \left(1 + \frac{x}{100}\right)^3 = \frac{125}{64} $$

$$ 1 + \frac{x}{100} = \frac{5}{4} \implies x = 25 $$

$$ \text{Net } \%_{2018-19} = \left( \frac{135}{100} \times \frac{90}{100} \right) - 1 = 1.215 - 1 = 21.5\% $$

$$ \text{Req. Ratio} = 25 : 21.5 = 50 : 43 $$

Exam Takeaway: Ninja trick always wins! Examiner ne intentionally 243,000 aur 102,400 aise set kiye hain ki ratio directly 27 aur 9 ke multiple me kate aur end me perfect cube 125/64 bache. Kabhi bhi intermediate exact numbers mat nikalna, seedha fraction ka chain kaato aur answer tik karo!

Data Trap TypeTestRipper Approach (Right)
Complex Intermediate ValuesDirectly chaining multipliers & moving backward
Final Ask CombinationIgnoring real values; using pure % successive change formula

questions.q: In the year 2014, the population of a city was 30,000. The population of the city increased in 2015, 2016 and 2017 by a constant number. In the year 2018, if the population of the city was increased by 20% over the previous year then the population of the city become 27600 more than that of the year 2014. What is the ratio of the percentage increase in the population of the city over the previous year in the year 2015 to that in the year 2017 over the previous year?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, "constant number" matlab AP chal rahi hai. 2018 ki population $2014 + 27600$ se aayegi, phir $20\%$ back karke 2017 ka pata chalega. Reverse calculations kar mentally.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Reverse series laga aur yearly increase nikal. Mathematically :-

$P_{2018} = 30000 + 27600 = 57600$

$P_{2017} = \frac{57600}{1.2} = 48000$

$\text{Inc in 3 yrs} = 48000 - 30000 = 18000 \Rightarrow \text{6000 per yr}$

$\%_{2015} = \frac{6000}{30000} = \frac{1}{5}$

$\%_{2017} = \frac{6000}{42000} = \frac{1}{7}$

$\text{Ratio} = \frac{1}{5} : \frac{1}{7} = 7 : 5$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Variables assume karke AP ka formula chalao. Mathematically :-

$P_{2014} = 30000$

$P_{2017} = 30000 + 3d$

$(30000 + 3d) \times 1.2 = 57600$

$30000 + 3d = 48000 \Rightarrow 3d = 18000 \Rightarrow d = 6000$

$\frac{6000}{30000} : \frac{6000}{30000+2(6000)} = \frac{1}{5} : \frac{1}{7} = 7:5$

Exam Takeaway: Constant increase humesha Arithmetic Progression (AP) hota hai, pichhe se backward aana smart move hai.

List IList II
AP Logic$\text{Value} = a + (n-1)d$

questions.q: Out of total income a person's expenditure on food, cloth and other items are in the ratio of 3: 4: 3 respectively. If his expenditure is increased by 12% on food and 15% on cloth and decreased by 8% on other items. What percent should his income be increased so that no effect is recorded on the consumption of food, cloth and other items ?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM/Deviation.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, ratios di hain 3:4:3. Inko sidha 300, 400 aur 300 maan le. Income base 1000 banega. Bas change nikal aur 1000 pe percentage fenk.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Zeroes assum kar aur base 1000 pe deviation nikal. Mathematically :-

$+ (300 \times 12\%) = +36$

$+ (400 \times 15\%) = +60$

$- (300 \times 8\%) = -24$

$\text{Net} = 36 + 60 - 24 = +72$

$\text{Inc } \% = \frac{72}{1000} \times 100 = 7.2\%$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Weighted average approach laga fraction me. Mathematically :-

$\text{Total parts} = 3+4+3 = 10$

$\text{Change} = \frac{(3 \times 12) + (4 \times 15) + (3 \times -8)}{10}$

$\text{Change} = \frac{36 + 60 - 24}{10} = \frac{72}{10} = 7.2\%$

Exam Takeaway: Jaha split ratio di ho waha zeros chipka ke life aasan kiya kar ya direct weighted average laga, fraction apne aap set hoga.

List IList II
Weighted Deviation$\frac{\sum (R_i \times \%_i)}{\sum R_i}$

questions.q: If x% of a is the same as y% of b, then z% of b will be
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, sidha equate karna hai. $x \times a = y \times b$. Hamein equation ko $b$ se form karni padegi aur pucha gaya expression satisfy karna hoga.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): $b$ ko a ke terms me substitute kar. Mathematically :-

$x \times a = y \times b \Rightarrow b = \frac{xa}{y}$

$\text{Req: } z\% \times b = z\% \times (\frac{xa}{y})$

$= (\frac{zx}{y})\% \text{ of } a$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Saare $100$ base ke sath equations solve kar. Mathematically :-

$\frac{x}{100} \times a = \frac{y}{100} \times b$

$b = \frac{a \times x}{y}$

$\text{Now } \frac{z}{100} \times b = \frac{z}{100} \times \frac{ax}{y}$

$= \frac{zx}{y \times 100} \times a = (\frac{zx}{y})\% \text{ of } a$

Exam Takeaway: Aise variable sawalon se darna nahi, jo pucha jaye directly usme term ko substitute kiya karo.

List IList II
Substitution$A = B \Rightarrow f(A) = f(B)$

questions.q: In an examination a candidate must secure 40% marks to pass. A candidate, who gets 220 marks, fails by 20 marks. What are the maximum marks for the examination?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, ekdum zero level sawal. 220 laaya, 20 se fail ho gaya. Matlab pass 240 pe the. Seedha $40\%$ ki value 240 se link kar.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Seedha equating kar without formula. Mathematically :-

$40\% = 220 + 20$

$40\% = 240$

$10\% = 60$

$100\% = 600$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Variable x rakh kar pura equation likh. Mathematically :-

$\text{Max Marks} = x$

$\frac{40}{100} \times x = 220 + 20$

$\frac{2}{5}x = 240$

$x = 240 \times \frac{5}{2} = 600$

Exam Takeaway: Passing marks hamesha equate hone chahiye (Marks obtained + Margin = Pass %).

List IList II
Equating Check$P_{marks} = \text{Score} + \text{Deficit}$

questions.q: A person invests 35% of his income in mutual funds, 25% in fixed deposits, and the rest in recurring deposits. After 2 years, the mutual funds grow by 20%, fixed deposits by 10% and recurring deposits by 15%. If his total income is Rs. 1,60,000, what is the total percentage return on his entire investment portfolio after 2 years?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM/Deviation.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, jab end mein 'percentage return' pucha hai toh actual income 1,60,000 ka koi role hi nahi bacha. Bas 100 maan kar returns nikal.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Weighted average laga bina absolute numbers use kiye. Mathematically :-

$MF = 35\%, FD = 25\%, RD = 40\%$

$\text{Ret}_{MF} = 35 \times 0.20 = 7$

$\text{Ret}_{FD} = 25 \times 0.10 = 2.5$

$\text{Ret}_{RD} = 40 \times 0.15 = 6$

$\text{Total Return} = 7 + 2.5 + 6 = 15.5$

$\text{Over 100} = 15.5\%$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Pura 1,60,000 pe pehle amounts nikal, fir returns laa (which is stupid). Mathematically :-

$MF = 160000 \times 0.35 = 56000 \Rightarrow 20\% = 11200$

$FD = 160000 \times 0.25 = 40000 \Rightarrow 10\% = 4000$

$RD = 160000 \times 0.40 = 64000 \Rightarrow 15\% = 9600$

$\text{Total Ret} = 24800$

$\% = \frac{24800}{160000} \times 100 = 15.5\%$

Exam Takeaway: Real values exam me bait karne ke liye hoti hain. Answer percentage mein ho toh hamesha percentage base pe khelo.

List IList II
Data Illusion$\text{Ignore absolute values}$

questions.q: A scholarship fund of Rs. 1200 is to be distributed between two students, A and B, in a ratio 5:3. However, after allocating 200 to administrative charges, the remaining amount is first increased by 10% as a bonus before the final division. What amount will student A receive? (PHASE XIII(HS) - 24/07/2025 - SHIFT 2)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, amount me se directly deduction aur bonus calculate karke final pool alag kar. Us pool ka $\frac{5}{8}$ seedha A ka hissa banega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Final pool ko direct fraction multiplier ke sath jod de. Mathematically :-

$\text{Pool} = (1200 - 200) \times 1.10 = 1100$

$A_{share} = 1100 \times \frac{5}{8}$

$A_{share} = 1100 \times 0.625 = 687.5$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Har step alag solve kar aur unit value nikal kar multiply kar. Mathematically :-

$\text{Rem} = 1200 - 200 = 1000$

$\text{Final} = 1000 + 10\% = 1100$

$\text{Total parts} = 5+3 = 8 \Rightarrow 8 \text{ parts } = 1100$

$1 \text{ part } = 137.5$

$A = 5 \times 137.5 = 687.5$

Exam Takeaway: Ratio ke final value ko parts me todne se behtar seedha multiplier se fraction multiply kar diya kar.

List IList II
Proportional Shift$A = \text{Total} \times \frac{A_{ratio}}{\sum \text{Ratios}}$

questions.q: In a contest held all over the country, 185 contestants won prizes after participating in the final round. 60% of the contestants could not make it to the final round. If 63% of the people participating in the final round did not win any prizes, then how many people participated in the contest?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, final round mein prize nahi jeetne wale $63\%$ hain, matlab jeetne wale bache $37\%$. Unki value $185$ (exact $5 \times 37$) di hai. Mentally reverse chal.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Reverse chain method laga bina kisi variable (x) ke. Mathematically :-

$\text{Final Winners } \% = 100 - 63 = 37\%$

$37\% = 185 \Rightarrow 100\% (\text{Finalists}) = 500$

$\text{Made to Final } \% = 100 - 60 = 40\%$

$40\% \text{ of Total} = 500$

$\text{Total} = \frac{500 \times 100}{40} = 1250$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Variable tree lagakar single equation solve kar. Mathematically :-

$\text{Total} = x$

$\text{Finalists} = 0.40x$

$\text{Winners} = 0.37 \times (0.40x) = 185$

$0.148x = 185$

$x = \frac{185}{0.148} = 1250$

Exam Takeaway: Jaha value chain ke end mein di ho waha backwards jana aur seedhi values banana best hota hai.

List IList II
Reverse Chain$\text{Start from End Value}$

questions.q: The total number of male and female population in a city increased by 25% from 1970 to 1980. During the same period, the male population increased by 40% while the female population increased by 20%. From 1980 to 1990, the female population increased by 25%. In 1990, if the female population is twice the male population, then the percentage increase in the total of male and female population in the city from 1970 to 1990 is.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM/Deviation.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, individual growth (M=40, F=20) aur overall (25) ek sath dekhte hi deemag mein alligation bajna chahiye. Ratio $1:3$ aayega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Alligation se base ratio nikal kar numbers assume kar. Mathematically :-

$\text{Alligation (1970): } M(40) \text{ & } F(20) \rightarrow Mix(25)$

$\text{Ratio } M:F = (25-20):(40-25) = 5:15 = 1:3$

$\text{Let } 1970: M=100, F=300 \Rightarrow \text{Total } = 400$

$\text{In } 1980: M = 140, F = 360$

$\text{In } 1990: F = 360 \times 1.25 = 450$

$M = \frac{450}{2} = 225 \Rightarrow \text{Total } 1990 = 675$

$\text{Inc } = \frac{675 - 400}{400} \times 100 = \frac{275}{4} = 68.75\%$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Variable based alligation equations likh. Mathematically :-

$\frac{0.4M + 0.2F}{M+F} = 0.25$

$0.4M + 0.2F = 0.25M + 0.25F \Rightarrow 0.15M = 0.05F \Rightarrow F = 3M$

$\text{1980}: M_1 = 1.4M, F_1 = 1.2(3M) = 3.6M$

$\text{1990}: F_2 = 1.25(3.6M) = 4.5M$

$M_2 = \frac{4.5M}{2} = 2.25M$

$\text{Total}_{1990} = 4.5M + 2.25M = 6.75M$

$\text{Inc} = \frac{6.75M - 4M}{4M} = \frac{2.75}{4} = 68.75\%$

Exam Takeaway: Jaha bhi combine average aur individual averages diye hon, Alligation method ko bina soche apply maar diya kar.

List IList II
Alligation Rule$\frac{N_1}{N_2} = \frac{A_m - A_2}{A_1 - A_m}$
